title: Claude + Blender MCP
author: fhtiek
selftext:
Been using the Blender MCP with Claude lately and am having a pretty difficult time, was hoping others might have some tips.

I had a relatively complicated creature to rig, lot of limbs on an eldritch monster. Claude managed to rig this decently well but it took a tremendous amount of manual effort correcting its bad habits. It took me nearly 2 days to get a working rig and I am still finding major shortcomings in it as i go. 

The trouble really is with animation. I never expected claude to animate well from scratch, but I did figure if I assembled key poses on the timeline it could interpolate and add anticipation and follow through and make some irganic adjustments. 

What Im finding is it goes completely rogue on me. I had a basic arm swing attack, manually animated all of it and then asked claude to do 2 simple things:

"As the swing begins, lead the motion with the root of the arm chain and have the tip of the arm chain follow slightly behind, creating a gentle trailing arc in the bone chain. Use our existing bezier curve follow control for this."

"When the swing reaches the end of it follow through on the forward swing, add a slight windup of anticipation just before the swing changes direction into the backswing. Invert the trailing arc shape of the forward swing on the backswing, again using the bezier curve follow control"

I gave the exact frames where actions happen. It would not do it. It would often do a lot of other things than what I asked. It started raising both arms in the air, it started rotating the root of the model, it at one point added several new bones which caused a bunch of random rippling. It just seemed to do anything and everything other than what I asked. I eventually had to give up and just had it simplify my keyframes into curves and just animated by hand.

Am I missing something? I have have perfect success using claude to animate bbmodels for minecraft, its been very useful. But in blender its just clueless and erratic. 

Are they skills I should be using? Am I just expecting too much? I figured it would be a good polish tool for making small changes to finished animations but right now Im lost. Any tips?

comments.author: BIGCHUG1404
comments.body: Are you giving it picture evidence? The AI does a whole lot better if you screenshot and circle what you’re talking about with a big red paintbrush in something like MS Paint. Even something like drawing the correct skeleton overtop the image with directional arrows for the attack is better than using only words for prompting. Now, you might very well already be doing this, but I would imagine that could possibly help if you aren’t.

replies.author: fhtiek
replies.body: I didnt think of drawing vector arrows for swing directions thats a good call. What i do in blender is just select groups of bones to reference limbs, ir oritent the scene camera at the specific area in question

comments.author: SideQuest_Builds
comments.body: might help to ask for one change per prompt and tell it exactly which bones it's allowed to key. two changes at once on a rig with that many limbs is probably where it starts messing with keys you already set

comments.author: magic-studios-admin
comments.body: Try out mixar . Agent centric cut of blender. Has worked pretty well for me
